students.n: SUMS (Students' Union Management System Ltd) incl. SU+ rewards and SU App
students.sum: Reward cards and benefits set up in a Rewards module (SU+ tiers such as Gold and Silver shown in the app listing);
students.cat:
Classification: Institutional / university benefits platform
Software platform used by students' unions: website, membership, events and EPOS, plus a branded SU App. SU+ is a rewards/loyalty module with reward cards and benefits, and members get a QR member pass. UK (listing address: Lincoln).
students.aud: Students' unions are the customers; their members (students) use the SU App.
students.acc: SU buys the platform. Students log in through their own Students' Union; SU+ memberships can be free or purchased.
students.ben: Reward cards and benefits set up in a Rewards module (SU+ tiers such as Gold and Silver shown in the app listing); digital member pass with QR code; event tickets; app home-screen tiles.
students.net:
SU customers cited: Oxford Brookes, Newcastle, Northampton, Westminster (testimonials on sums.su); trade press adds Edinburgh, Reading and Imperial College Union. Over twenty unions use the platform; which of them switch on the SU+ rewards module is not verified.
SUMS clients named on sums.digital (Nov 2026; CRM and SU app, SU+ rewards module is optional): Lincoln, Nottingham, Kent, Hull, Sussex, Sheffield, York, York St John, Northampton, Oxford Brookes, Loughborough, Bishop Grosseteste, Newcastle, Westminster, Manchester, Edinburgh, Northumbria, Bath Spa, Reading, City St George's.
students.sw: Strengths: one platform reaches many SUs and already has loyalty-card and QR-pass mechanics. Weaknesses: SU-branded and SU-owned data; no retailer discount network of its own; rolled out SU by SU.
students.mw: Best SU distribution route found in this run: one partnership or integration could place Membership Wallet cards and offers inside many SU apps. SU+ is also a template for SU-branded loyalty cards that MW could host.
students.rat: 4/5 — High. Rubric (benefit upside 4, tap ease 3, reach 4, evidence 4). Tap route: Integrate. Permissions: vendor partnership; one agreement can reach many unions.

affReadme: How to use: most UK retailers do not publish their own public API. Their sales, vouchers, product feeds and promotions are exposed through the affiliate network they run their programme on.

1) Join the network listed in 'Usual affiliate route' (free publisher account). 2) Apply to that retailer's programme inside the network. 3) Use the network's API (link in the row) to pull that retailer's offers, vouchers and product feeds.

Bank developer portals are Open Banking (account/payment data) — bank cashback offers (Barclaycard, Lloyds Everyday Offers, NatWest MyRewards, Santander Boosts) run via Cardlytics / card-linked platforms, not open APIs.
Network assignment reflects the usual/primary UK programme; brands move networks, so confirm on the network's advertiser directory when applying.
Where no public API exists, the link points to the brand's site — use its Help/Contact page (footer) or the brand's affiliate/partnerships page.
Developer portal links for networks, banks and card-linked platforms were checked via web search; links could not be live-tested from this environment.

offers.title: UK Retailer & Offer Data Sources
offers.purpose: Identify where Membership Wallet can get UK retailer details and their offers by API, what each source provides, and whether one source can cover everything.
findings: Each source covers one part: affiliate networks give online deals, Fidel gives in-store offers, gift card providers give rewards, and location datasets give store details. See the Capability Matrix.
Most sources give name, logo, website and category only. Store addresses, opening hours and contacts need Google Places, open map data or the retailer directly.
3. Awin is the best starting point.
Largest UK network, public Offers API, free to join, and earns commission from day one.
Its only API syncs HR data. It is a competitor and benchmark, not a data source.
5. Companies House is free and useful.
Use it to verify that retailers are real, active UK companies during onboarding.

notes: Verification

Each source is marked in the Sources sheet as verified from provider documentation, a well-documented public API, or general knowledge to confirm. Confirm exact fields with each provider before building.
Approval times
Indicative estimates, not published figures. They depend on each provider’s review and on having a live app.
Costs
Based on public information as of November 2026. Most affiliate networks are free for publishers; aggregators take a share of commission; gift card providers need a contract and prefunded balance.
Retailer coverage
Every network only includes retailers that have joined it. A retailer not on Awin will not appear in Awin’s data.
Data licences
Google Places limits data storage and requires attribution. OpenStreetMap requires attribution and share-alike (ODbL). Check licence terms before storing data.
Amazon Associates
Its operating agreement restricts rebates and incentives on purchases, which may rule out loyalty or cashback use.
Regulation
Paying withdrawable cashback could affect the FCA position in your licences register. Take regulatory advice before launching cashback.
Data protection
Card linking (Fidel) needs explicit member consent under UK GDPR and should be covered by the DPIA.
Scraping
Scraping retailer or voucher websites is not recommended: it usually breaches their terms and earns no commission.
Perkbox
Research found no public Perkbox offers API. Its integrations sync HR data (name, email, employment status, team) from systems like Workday, HiBob and BambooHR.
Editing
Suitability values in the Sources sheet use a drop-down; the Summary counts update automatically.
